Alpair 5G Loudspeaker
Anechoic Chamber Test Report1 m Baffle Test and 240 mm Simulation

This report documents the Alpair 5G anechoic chamber measurements recorded on 17 October 2026. It includes the 1 m baffle test and 240 mm simulation, setup photographs, frequency response, total harmonic distortion and measurement summaries.

01

Test Scope and Conditions

CONFIGURATION A

1 m baffle measurement

The Alpair 5G loudspeaker was mounted in a baffle inside the anechoic chamber. One frequency-response and total-harmonic-distortion sweep was recorded.

Distance
1 m, matching the datasheet measurement distance specified for this test.
Exported range
Approximately 19–40000 Hz.
Test settings
The acquisition screenshot shows a generator setting of 286 mVrms and EQ set to None.

286 mVrms is the generator setting. Matching the measurement distance does not establish numerical agreement with the datasheet response.

CONFIGURATION B

240 mm anechoic chamber simulation

The measurement log assigns 18 tests to 10 groups: 70 dB before and after EQ, followed by measurements after EQ at the other nominal sound pressure levels.

Distance
240 mm.
Nominal SPL
40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 93, 96 and 98 dB.
Exported range
Frequency response: 50–10000 Hz; THD: 25–10000 Hz.

Nominal SPL identifies the test setting. The measured sound pressure level varies with frequency.

03

Measurement Parameters and Reference Limits

Frequency: the horizontal axis

Frequency is shown in Hz, from low to high. Logarithmic spacing gives 100–1000 Hz the same width as 1000–10000 Hz.

Response: sound pressure level

RMS Level shows the measured level at each frequency in dB SPL. Compare the trace with the target level and its upper and lower limits.

Distortion: THD

Total harmonic distortion is expressed as a percentage. A trace above a red dashed reference line exceeds that reference at the corresponding frequency.

EQ: equalization

EQ adjusts gain across frequencies to change the response. Read the before-EQ and after-EQ results under their respective test conditions.

Axis tick labels use ordinary integers, without scientific notation. The actual 0.3% reference and fractional SPL limits are retained and identified in the legends.

07

Test Conclusions

English translation of the conclusions supplied by the test author.

In the anechoic chamber, the interference-related peak around 1 kHz in the distortion response disappears.

Distortion is somewhat lower than inside the test box. However, the 70 dB results still do not fully meet the customer's requirement of less than 0.3%.

The 93–98 dB tests confirm that these higher sound pressure levels exceed the loudspeaker's performance limits. As the level increases, more of the equalized frequency response falls outside the limit envelope, and a larger portion of the distortion response exceeds 1%.

Overall, the loudspeaker's response performance progressively deteriorates as sound pressure level increases. Performance also worsens as the level approaches approximately 40 dB.

Corresponding report: Alpair 5G Loudspeaker — Anechoic Chamber Test Report, 17 October 2026, 31 pages.

Sources: Excel measurement exports, acquisition screenshots, test records and setup photographs from the 1 m baffle test and the 240 mm simulation. These plots use the same exported samples as the report and retain the original numerical precision.

Reading and sharing: Plot segments connect actual samples. Move over or tap a plot to inspect the nearest sample. Tables display values to two or three decimal places. All photographs and chart data are included in this file, which can be opened offline.
